hook.line: Every transaction has two directions: someone hands something over and someone picks it up. Vale sends out cakes all week, and in Bogotá a delivery is a *domicilio*.
hook.es: Le entregamos el pedido a domicilio.
hook.en: We deliver your (formal) order to your door.

examples.es: Paso a recoger los documentos el viernes.
examples.en: I'll come by to pick up the documents on Friday.

examples.es: Le entregamos el pedido a domicilio.
examples.en: We deliver your (formal) order to your door.

examples.es: Recojo a los niños a las cuatro.
examples.en: I pick the children up at four.

examples.es: Ya le entregué las llaves al dueño.

examples.es: El domiciliario entregó el pedido a las ocho.
examples.en: The delivery rider handed over the order at eight.
Mariana picks up the documents tomorrow.

rule:
*Entregar* is to hand over or deliver. The thing is the object, and who receives it comes with *le* or *a*: *Le entregué las llaves al dueño*.

*Recoger* goes the other way: to pick up, for things (*los documentos*) or people (*a los niños*, with *a* before the person).

*Paso a recoger* means "I'll drop by to pick up".

*A domicilio* means to your door. In Colombia *un domicilio* is a delivery and *el domiciliario* is the rider.
smallPrint: Teachers call the *a* before *los niños* the personal *a*: it marks a person as the object.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Paso a ___ los documentos el viernes.* (*recoger* or *entregar*) I'll come by to pick up the documents on Friday.
yourTurn.answer: Paso a recoger los documentos el viernes.
yourTurn.why: You come by to collect them, so *recoger*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Le ___ el pedido a domicilio.* (*entregamos* or *recogemos*) We deliver your order to your door.
yourTurn.answer: Le entregamos el pedido a domicilio.
yourTurn.why: Handing it over to the customer is *entregar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I pick the children up at four.
yourTurn.answer: Recojo a los niños a las cuatro.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I already handed the keys over to the owner.
yourTurn.answer: Ya le entregué las llaves al dueño.
yourTurn.why: The person who receives it comes with *le* and *al*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The delivery rider handed over the order at eight.
yourTurn.answer: El domiciliario entregó el pedido a las ocho.
yourTurn.why: *Entregó* is the *he* or *she* form in the past.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *we*: *Recojo a los niños a las cuatro.*
yourTurn.answer: Recogemos a los niños a las cuatro.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it around so you hand it over: *Paso a recoger los documentos el viernes.*
yourTurn.answer: Paso a entregar los documentos el viernes.

pitfalls.wrong: Recojo los niños a las cuatro.
pitfalls.right: Recojo a los niños a las cuatro.
pitfalls.why: A person as the object needs *a*, so *a los niños*.

pitfalls.wrong: Ya entregué las llaves para el dueño.
pitfalls.right: Ya le entregué las llaves al dueño.
pitfalls.why: English "to" tempts *para*, but the person who receives something takes *a* (here *al*), usually with *le* too.
*Pasar* needs *a* before the verb that says why you drop by.

personal: Think of something you have to pick up or hand over this week and say it: *Tengo que recoger…* or *Voy a entregar…*
